channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Chiefs HC Andy Reid said the team is “leaning against” playing Patrick Mahomes in next week’s preseason opener.
ESPN’s Kevin Seifert says there have been “plenty of indications that Kyler Murray remains the heavy favorite” to win the Vikings’ starting QB job.
item.description: According to Seifert, the Vikings have given Murray “roughly two-thirds of the snaps with the first-team offense in 11-on-11 drills,” while J.J. McCarthy “has spent a significant portion of his summer working with the No. 2 offense.” While reports have been up and down on Murray thus far, Seifert also suggests the gap between Murray and McCarthy remains wide after the first two weeks of camp, saying that “no objective observer to training camp could say that (McCarthy) has made up the ground necessary to truly challenge Murray” this summer. There are still two weeks left to go in camp, but it sounds like McCarthy will need a lot to go right for him to get the nod for Week 1 against the Packers.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan believes Giants WR Malachi Fields “has made an early claim for the No. 2 receiver spot” in camp.
item.description: The Giants traded up to select Fields with the No. 74 overall pick in this year’s draft, adding him to a receiver room that is noticeably thin behind Malik Nabers. This isn’t the first time Fields has garnered praise from the media, as ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported in late July that the Giants were “highly impressed” by the hulking receiver who made a name for himself as a contested catch specialist. It’s highly unlikely that Fields will make enough of an impact as a rookie to be a viable fantasy option, but he could prove valuable as a big target in and around the end zone for the Giants this season.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Cyrus Allen (shin) returned to practice on Friday.
item.description: Allen has been sidelined since Saturday after he suffered a shin injury during a collision with a teammate. The flashy fifth-round rookie has made a name for himself in the early part of training camp and is now back on the field following his brief injury scare. Allen’s recent training camp hype has made him an interesting dart throw in the later rounds of drafts, but it will likely take a few things breaking in his favor for him to make a meaningful fantasy impact this season.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Falcons released LB Troy Andersen.
item.description: The Falcons selected Andersen with the 58th overall pick in 2022, but the veteran linebacker has appeared in just 26 games since entering the league. Injuries have plagued Andersen for much of his career; a shoulder/pec injury ended his 2023 campaign in Week 3, and a knee injury he suffered in 2024 limited him to seven games that season and sidelined him for all of last year. As a rookie, Andersen totaled 69 tackles and three TFLs. He is now free to sign with any team as he looks to get his career back on track.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Texans activated WR Jaylin Noel (finger) from the active/NFI list.
item.description: Noel started camp on the NFI list after suffering a finger injury away from the team. The second-year receiver is now back with the team and will face stiff competition for playing time with Tank Dell now back and Xavier Hutchinson and Jayden Higgins also working with the first-team offense. Noel caught 26 passes for 292 yards and two touchdowns in 17 games as a rookie.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Bills signed OG O’Cyrus Torrence to a four-year, $78.4 million contract extension.
item.description: A former second-round pick from the 2023 draft class, Torrence has appeared in all 51 regular-season games for the Bills since entering the league. He has started all but one of those games in his career, appearing on over 3,300 snaps. Head coach Joe Brady praised Torrence for being “one of the top guards in football,” as the Bills have now locked him in through the 2030 season. Torrence’s deal includes $46 million in guaranteed money.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Colts coach Shane Steichen said there remains no timetable for Alec Pierce’s (left ankle surgery) return.
item.description: “No, not right now,” was Steichen’s response when asked if there was a timeline. “His rehab’s going great, I’ll say that. ... I don’t have the timetable on his return, but he’s doing a hell of a job in his rehab process.” “No timeline” might be a bit disingenuous, but probably no more so than when GM Chris Ballard said nine days ago Pierce was a “week or two” from returning. The Colts’ brain trust is being intentionally vague, but we still haven’t seen anything to suggest Week 1 is off the table. On the other hand, we’ve seen nothing to suggest it is assured. Pierce’s status is genuinely up in the air, making him a high-risk WR3 in August fantasy drafts.-Patrick Daugherty

item.title: Cardinals QB Carson Beck completed 15-of-19 passes for 188 yards and a touchdown in Thursday’s Hall-of-Fame Game against the Panthers.
item.description: Beck played two-plus quarters. No offense to the Hall-of-Fame Game, but it’s not a contest we typically go into expecting highlights. The Cardinals’ No. 3 quarterback provided several of them, hitting Jalen Brooks for a 49-yard deep strike and Simi Fehoko for a five-yard end zone fade touchdown. In between were several smart in-rhythm completions, with Beck navigating the pocket well. 24-year-old Beck’s arm strength remains a massive question mark — even his Brooks completion drifted a bit toward the middle of the field — but his processing was on point against the Panthers’ second- and third-team defense. Although he was a highly polarizing pre-draft prospect, the fact that the rebuilding Cardinals were willing to use a Day 2 selection strongly suggests he will make late-season starts as the organization keeps an eye on the future.-Patrick Daugherty

item.title: Rams coach Sean McVay said it’s too early to say whether retired DT Aaron Donald will return this season.
item.description: With un-retirement rumors swirling for months, Donald officially worked out for the team earlier this week. "(Donald is) feeling good, but we’re not to where we are able to say whether or not he is or isn’t ready to do it,” McVay said Thursday. “But he’s doing great and he looked outstanding (in Tuesday’s workout), as I think all of us would expect.” At this point, we wouldn’t be surprised if the sides simply had a wink-nod agreement to wait to formalize any return until training camp is over. Training camp is the bane of many veteran players’ existence, and the Rams would undoubtedly trust Donald to suit up and be effective without going through the August rigamarole. Of course, it’s also possible a 35-year-old who has spent two years away from the game ultimately decides he’s better off not getting back in the saddle. Stay tuned.-Patrick Daugherty
